CPSC 100.title: Computational Thinking
CPSC 100.description: Meaning and impact of computational thinking. Solving problems using computational thinking, testing, debugging. How computers work. No prior computing experience required. Not for students with existing credit for or exemption from CPSC 107, CPSC 110 or APSC 160.

CPSC 103.title: Introduction to Systematic Program Design
CPSC 103.description: Computation as a tool for systematic problem solving in non-computer-science disciplines. Introductory programming skills. Not for credit for students who have credit for, or exemption from, or are concurrently taking CPSC 110 or APSC 160. No programming experience expected.

CPSC 107.title: Systematic Program Design
CPSC 107.description: Fundamental computation and program structures. Continuing systematic program design from CPSC 103.

CPSC 110.title: Computation, Programs, and Programming
CPSC 110.description: Fundamental program and computation structures. Introductory programming skills. Computation as a tool for information processing, simulation and modelling, and interacting with the world.

CPSC 121.title: Models of Computation
CPSC 121.description: Physical and mathematical structures of computation. Boolean algebra and combinations logic circuits; proof techniques; functions and sequential circuits; sets and relations; finite state machines; sequential instruction execution.

CPSC 203.title: Programming, Problem Solving, and Algorithms
CPSC 203.description: Analysis of increasingly complex algorithmic problems, using a modern programming language and a variety of approaches. Problem decomposition and abstraction guide explorations of topics from applied algorithms, for example Voronoi Diagrams, Markov Chains, Bin Packing, and Graph Search. Not for students with credit for, or currently enrolled in, CPSC 210 or CPEN 221.
CPSC 203.prerequisiteText: One of CPSC 103, CPSC 110, APSC 160, EOSC 211, MATH 210, PHYS 210, COMM 337

CPSC 210.title: Software Construction
CPSC 210.description: Design, development, and analysis of robust software components. Topics such as software design, computational models, data structures, debugging, and testing.

CPSC 213.title: Introduction to Computer Systems
CPSC 213.description: Software architecture, operating systems, and I/O architectures. Relationships between application software, operating systems, and computing hardware; critical sections, deadlock avoidance, and performance; principles and operation of disks and networks.

CPSC 221.title: Basic Algorithms and Data Structures
CPSC 221.description: Design and analysis of basic algorithms and data structures; algorithm analysis methods, searching and sorting algorithms, basic data structures, graphs and concurrency.

children.raw: a score of 68% or higher in

CPSC 221.prerequisiteText: One of CPSC_V 210, CPEN_V 221 and either (a) one of CPSC_V 121, MATH_V 220, MATH_O 220 or (b) a score of 68% or higher in MATH_V 226

CPSC 259.title: Data Structures and Algorithms for Electrical Engineers
CPSC 259.description: Advanced procedural programming. Fundamental algorithms for sorting and searching. Data structures including lists, trees, and hash tables. Introduction to scripting languages and file input/output.

CPSC 298.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
CPSC 298.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in the computing industry for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during Winter Session of second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Computer Science.

CPSC 299.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
CPSC 299.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in the computing industry for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer following the second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education.

CPSC 302.title: Numerical Computation for Algebraic Problems
CPSC 302.description: Numerical techniques for basic mathematical processes involving no discretization, and their analysis. Solution of linear systems, including analysis of round-off errors; norms and condition number; introduction to iterative techniques in linear algebra, including eigenvalue problems; solution to nonlinear equations.
CPSC 302.prerequisiteText: One of CPSC 103, CPSC 110, CPEN 221, EOSC 211, PHYS 210 and one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223

CPSC 303.title: Numerical Approximation and Discretization
CPSC 303.description: Numerical techniques for basic mathematical processes involving discretization, and their analysis. Interpolation and approximation, including splines and least squares data fitting; numerical differentiation and integration; introduction to numerical initial value ordinary differential equations.
CPSC 303.prerequisiteText: One of CPSC 103, CPSC 110, CPEN 221, EOSC 211, PHYS 210 and one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223

CPSC 304.title: Introduction to Relational Databases
CPSC 304.description: Overview of database systems, ER models, logical database design and normalization, formal relational query languages, SQL and other commercial languages, data warehouses, special topics.

CPSC 310.title: Introduction to Software Engineering
CPSC 310.description: Specification, design, validation, evolution and construction of modern software systems, within the context of socially and professionally relevant domains such as ethics, intellectual property, and information security.

CPSC 311.title: Definition of Programming Languages
CPSC 311.description: Comparative study of advanced programming language features. Statement types, data types, variable binding, parameter passing mechanisms. Methods for syntactic and semantic description of programming languages.

CPSC 312.title: Functional and Logic Programming
CPSC 312.description: Principles of symbolic computing, using languages based upon first-order logic and the lambda calculus. Algorithms for implementing such languages. Applications to artificial intelligence and knowledge representation.

CPSC 313.title: Computer Hardware and Operating Systems
CPSC 313.description: Instruction sets, pipelining, code optimization, caching, virtual memory management, dynamically linked libraries, exception processing, execution time of programs.
CPSC 313.prerequisiteText: CPSC_V 213 and either CPSC_V 221 or DSCI_V 221

CPSC 314.title: Computer Graphics
CPSC 314.description: Human vision and colour; geometric transformations; algorithms for 2-D and 3-D graphics; hardware and system architectures; shading and lighting; animation.
CPSC 314.prerequisiteText: CPSC_V 221 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_O 200 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222

CPSC 317.title: Introduction to Computer Networking
CPSC 317.description: Computer networking, basic communication protocols, network infrastructure and routing. Common application-level protocols and principles associated with developing distributed applications.
CPSC 317.prerequisiteText: CPSC_V 213 and either CPSC_V 221 or DSCI_V 221

CPSC 319.title: Software Engineering Project
CPSC 319.description: The design, implementation, and test of a large software system, using a team approach.

CPSC 320.title: Intermediate Algorithm Design and Analysis
CPSC 320.description: Systematic study of basic concepts and techniques in the design and analysis of algorithms, illustrated from various problem areas. Topics include models of computation; choice of data structures; and graph-theoretic, algebraic, and text processing algorithms.

children.raw: at least 3 credits from MATH_V or STAT_V at 200 level or above

CPSC 320.prerequisiteText: All of (a) CPSC_V 221 or DSCI_V 221, (b) at least 3 credits from MATH_V or STAT_V at 200 level or above or MATH_O 200, MATH_O 220, MATH_O 222, MATH_O 225, MATH_O 307, STAT_O 121, STAT_O 203, STAT_O 205, STAT_O 230, STAT_O 303 or any course on the STAT_V 200 credit exclusion: or HES_O 340, HMKN_O 205, POLI_O 400, PSYO_O 271, STAT_O 124

CPSC 322.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
CPSC 322.description: Problem-solving and planning. State/action models and graph searching. Natural language understanding. Computational vision. Applications of artificial intelligence.

CPSC 330.title: Applied Machine Learning
CPSC 330.description: Application of machine learning tools, with an emphasis on solving practical problems. Data cleaning, feature extraction, supervised and unsupervised machine learning, reproducible workflows, and communicating results.
CPSC 330.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of CPSC_V 203, CPSC_V 210, CPEN_V 221, DSCI_V 221 or (b) MATH_V 210 and one of CPSC_V 107, CPSC_V 110

CPSC 337.title: Introduction to Computer Security
CPSC 337.description: Fundamentals of computer security and privacy. Cryptography, network security, and application security. Security assessments, problem diagnosis, defensive strategies. Impacts and outcomes of security design decisions.

CPSC 340.title: Machine Learning and Data Mining
CPSC 340.description: Models of algorithms for dimensionality reduction, nonlinear regression, classification, clustering and unsupervised learning; applications to computer graphics, computer games, bio-informatics, information retrieval, e-commerce, databases, computer vision and artificial intelligence.
CPSC 340.prerequisiteText: All of (a) one of CPSC_V 221, DSCI_V 221 (b) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222 (c) one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200 (d) one of STAT_V 241, STAT_V 251, ECON_V 325, ECON_V 327, MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, MATH_V 318, STAT_O 302

CPSC 344.title: Introduction to Human Computer Interaction Methods
CPSC 344.description: Basic tools and techniques, teaching a systematic approach to interface design, task analysis, analytic and empirical evaluation methods.

CPSC 349.title: Honours Research Seminar
CPSC 349.description: Students will attend a series of research seminars presented by faculty members, produce a thesis proposal, and choose their honours thesis supervisor. Available to Honours students. Majors students with satisfactory standing may also be permitted to enrol.

CPSC 368.title: Databases in Data Science
CPSC 368.description: Overview of relational and non-relational database systems, role and usage of a database when querying data, data modelling, query languages, and query optimization.
CPSC 368.prerequisiteText: One of CPSC_V 203, CPSC_V 210, CPEN_V 221, DSCI_V 221

CPSC 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
CPSC 398.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in the computing industry for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer following the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Computer Science.

CPSC 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
CPSC 399.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in the computing industry for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the fall term of the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Computer Science.

CPSC 402.title: Numerical Linear Algebra
CPSC 402.description: Investigation of the practical techniques of computational linear algebra. Orthogonal transformations and their application to the solution of linear equations, the eigenproblem, and linear least squares. Complete solution of the symmetric eigenproblem, including bisection and the QR method. Refinements of these techniques for sparse matrices.

CPSC 404.title: Advanced Relational Databases
CPSC 404.description: Physical database design, indexing, external mergesort, relational query processing and optimization, transaction processing, concurrency control, crash recovery, special topics.
CPSC 404.prerequisiteText: CPSC 304 and one of CPSC 213, CPSC 261, CPEN 212

CPSC 406.title: Computational Optimization
CPSC 406.description: Formulation and analysis of algorithms for continuous and discrete optimization problems; linear, nonlinear, network, dynamic, and integer optimization; large-scale problems; software packages and their implementation; duality theory and sensitivity.

CPSC 410.title: Advanced Software Engineering
CPSC 410.description: Specification, design, construction and validation of multi-version software systems.
CPSC 410.prerequisiteText: Either (a) CPSC 310 or (b) all of CPEN 321, CPEN 331

CPSC 411.title: Introduction to Compiler Construction
CPSC 411.description: A practical introduction to lexical analysis, syntactic analysis, type-checking, code generation and optimization. This will be used to design and implement a compiler for a small language.

CPSC 415.title: Operating Systems Design and Implementation
CPSC 415.description: Team-based design and implementation of a complete operating system, with emphasis on applicability to modern hardware and the practical implementation of operating systems concepts.
CPSC 415.prerequisiteText: All of the following with a minimum grade of 76% in each of: (a) CPSC_V 310 or CPEN_V 321, (b) CPSC_V 313 or CPEN_V 331, and (c) CPSC_V 317 or ELEC_V 331

CPSC 416.title: Distributed Systems
CPSC 416.description: Concepts and design of distributed systems. Communication architecture and models for interprocess communication. Process migration, naming, distributed file systems, fault tolerance, and concurrency control.
CPSC 416.prerequisiteText: One of CPSC 313, CPEN 331 and one of CPSC 317, ELEC 331

CPSC 417.title: Computer Networking
CPSC 417.description: Network protocols and architecture including internetworking, the Internet, layered communication protocols, routing, flow and congestion control, network performance, wired and wireless data communication.

CPSC 418.title: Parallel Computation
CPSC 418.description: Algorithms, architectures, and programming paradigms for parallel computation. Shared memory, message passing, and data parallel architectures and programming models. Parallel algorithms including reduce, scan, and sorting networks. Reasoning about the correctness of parallel programs. Performance analysis and measurement for parallel programs.
CPSC 418.prerequisiteText: CPSC 320 and one of CPSC 261, CPSC 313, CPEN 212, CPEN 411

CPSC 420.title: Advanced Algorithms Design and Analysis
CPSC 420.description: The study of advanced topics in the design and analysis of algorithms and associated data structures. Topics include algorithms for graph-theoretic; algebraic and geometric problems; algorithms on nonsequential models; complexity issues; approximation algorithms.

CPSC 421.title: Introduction to Theory of Computing
CPSC 421.description: Characterizations of computability (using machines, languages and functions). Universality, equivalence and Church's thesis. Unsolvable problems. Restricted models of computation. Finite automata, grammars and formal languages.
CPSC 421.prerequisiteText: One of CPSC 320 or MATH 220 or MATH 226

CPSC 423.title: Natural Language Processing
CPSC 423.description: Fundamentals of data-driven natural language processing, including applications (machine translation, summarization, question answering), text representations (word embeddings, language models), and statistical and neural-network methods.
CPSC 423.prerequisiteText: Either CPSC_V 340 or both (a) one of AI_V 240, CPSC_V 330 and (b) one of STAT_V 200, STAT_V 251, ECON_V 325, ECON_V 327, MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, MATH_V 318

CPSC 424.title: Geometric Modelling
CPSC 424.description: Digital representation of curves and surfaces, including splines, subdivision surfaces and meshes. Principles, algorithms and mathematical foundations for geometry representation in computer graphics, computer vision, fabrication, CAD/CAM, and medical imaging. Algorithms for acquisition, creation, representation, and processing of 3D shapes.
CPSC 424.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223 and one of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253

CPSC 425.title: Computer Vision
CPSC 425.description: Introduction to the processing and interpretation of images. Image sensing, sampling, and filtering. Algorithms for colour analysis, texture description, stereo imaging, motion interpretation, 3D shape recovery, and recognition.
CPSC 425.prerequisiteText: CPSC_V 221 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254 and one of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223

CPSC 426.title: Computer Animation
CPSC 426.description: Motion in computer graphics for characters and their environments. Keyframing, inverse kinematics, particle systems, rigid body dynamics, contact and collision, controller-based active motion, motion capture.

CPSC 427.title: Video Game Programming
CPSC 427.description: Video game programming techniques and technologies, including rendering, animation, interaction, game AI, real-time software development for games; start-to-finish simple video-game design and implementation. [1.5–1.5-1]
CPSC 427.prerequisiteText: CPSC_V 314 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223

CPSC 430.title: Computers and Society
CPSC 430.description: Impact of computer technology on society; historical perspectives; social and economic consequences of large-scale information processing systems and automatic control; legal and ethical problems in computer applications. Computers and the individual: machine versus human capabilities, fact and fancy; problematic interface between man and machine.

prerequisite.raw: 3 credits of Computer Science and at least third-year standing

CPSC 430.prerequisiteText: 3 credits of Computer Science and at least third-year standing

CPSC 436.title: Topics in Computer Science
CPSC 436.description: Selected topics in a specific area within Computer Science. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the department.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing in a Computer Science or Computer Engineering specialization, and permission of the department

CPSC 436.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing in a Computer Science or Computer Engineering specialization, and permission of the department

CPSC 440.title: Advanced Machine Learning
CPSC 440.description: Advanced machine learning techniques focusing on probabilistic models. Deep learning and differentiable programming, exponential families and Bayesian inference, probabilistic graphical models and other generative models, Monte Carlo and variational inference methods.
CPSC 440.prerequisiteText: Either CPSC_V 340 or both (a) AI_V 240 and (b) one of STAT_V 251, ECON_V 325, ECON_V 327, MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, MATH_V 318

CPSC 444.title: Advanced Methods for Human Computer Interaction
CPSC 444.description: Design and evaluation methodologies and theories; formal models of the user including visual, motor, and information processing; advanced evaluation methods including laboratory experiments and field studies; HCI research frontiers.
CPSC 444.prerequisiteText: CPSC 344 and one of STAT 200, STAT 201, STAT 203, STAT 241, STAT 251, BIOL 300, COMM 291, ECON 325, ECON 327, FRST 231, GEOG 374, KIN 206, KIN 371, POLI 380, PSYC 218, PSYC 278, PSYC 366, SOCI 328

CPSC 445.title: Algorithms in Bioinformatics
CPSC 445.description: Sequence alignment, phylogenetic tree reconstruction, prediction of RNA and protein structure, gene finding and sequence annotation, gene expression, and biomolecular computing.
CPSC 445.prerequisiteText: CPSC 320. and either BMEG 250 or six credits of BIOL beyond BIOL 111

CPSC 447.title: Introduction to Visualization
CPSC 447.description: Design and implementation of static and interactive visualizations. Selection of appropriate visualization methods for given combinations of data type and intended analysis task. Assessment of visual representations according to design and perceptual principles.

CPSC 448.title: Directed Studies in Computer Science
CPSC 448.description: Open ordinarily to students in Computer Science with at least a 72% average and permission of the department. The course may consist of supervised reading, participation in a seminar, and one or more programming projects.

CPSC 449.title: Honours Thesis
CPSC 449.description: Under supervision of a faculty member, students investigate a research topic and prepare a thesis.

CPSC 455.title: Applied Industry Practices
CPSC 455.description: Hands-on project, mentored by industry experts, integrating skills relevant to early career in the computing industry: technical skills, communication, teamwork, networking and portfolio building.

CPSC 490.title: Student Directed Seminars
CPSC 490.description: Self-directed, collaborative studies, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars.

CPSC 491.title: Interactive Digital Media Practicum
CPSC 491.description: Design and implementation of interactive digital media systems using modern processes and tools. Projects provided by external clients or vetted entrepreneurial pitches are developed by interdisciplinary teams composed of one CPSC_V 491 student and multiple Master of Digital Media students.
CPSC 491.prerequisiteText: All of CPSC_V 221, CPSC_V 310, CPSC_V 344 and Third-year standing

CPSC 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement V
CPSC 499.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in the computing industry for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer following the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Computer Science.

CPSC 500.title: Fundamentals of Algorithm Design and Analysis

CPSC 501.title: Theory of Automata, Formal Languages and Computability

CPSC 513.title: Introduction to Formal Verification and Analysis

CPSC 537.title: Topics in Coding and Information Theory

CPSC 541.title: Topics in Computer Security and Privacy

CPSC 543.title: Physical User Interface Design and Evaluation
